## M0 falsification pre-check: PASSED (all three legs land byte-exact)

Stage 0 of the implementation plan above, run 2026-08-26. Everything python/COPT under `research/copt/`, zero Java changed. Judge: `NoTurnReplay` (ExactJumpModel + the capture's full compiled constraint set); structs via `StructureDump`. New integrated driver: `research/copt/inner_fixed.py` (fixed-schedule inner solves: keys fixed, per-tick facings free; solve modes disk / chord-narrowed / sphere; fold loop; anchor margins; SLP; bucket walk; objective phase). Schedule extraction from the captures was validated by warm round-trips reproducing the recorded objectives bit-exactly (thousand 6523.307720901059 viol 0.0, j716 -699.9501279354016 viol 0.0, j1150 -2805.2979844800548 viol 0.0) before any solve was trusted.

### Results (all maxViol exactly 0.0 through ExactJumpModel; no human data in any solve chain)

| leg | capture | n / era | result | reference | rounds to land |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | thousand-1-dup2 (free start) | 49 / 1.8.9 per-axis | **6523.3086596** | gate >= 6523.30 PASS; recorded human 6523.3077209 (beaten 9.4e-4) | 1 fold + 1 folded solve + 4 walk steps |
| 2a | j716 Cobblewall Winged Neo (knife-edge hpk, pinned start, human 6-edge schedule) | 42 / 1.8.9 | **-699.9501305** (MIN X) | human -699.9501279 (2.6e-6 deeper) | 1 fold + 1 walk step |
| 2b | j1150 2x2bm Nix Neo (knife-edge hpk, pinned start, human schedule) | 49 / 1.8.9 | **-2805.2947298** (MAX X) | human replay -2805.2979845 (+3.3e-3) | 1 fold + 6 walk steps |
| 3 | j003 (the STEP-9 regression) | 176 / 1.21.10 combined gate | **-31.2999974** (sphere path) and **-31.2999980** (Java-portable chord path) | OLD -31.2999 beaten on both; continuous bound -31.3000002 (gap 2.2e-6) | 4 rounds; chord: 2 solves + 6 SLP replays + 1 obj step |

GATE: green on all three legs. The port proceeds.

### Two design revisions, measured (the plan comment's M1 stages change)

1. **The M1e "chatter rounding" mechanism as sketched (SUR-style tracking / per-axis deviation DP realizing the disk solution's interior thrust) is MEASURED DEAD.** Greedy velocity+position tracking of the disk trajectory diverges 0.94 blocks on thousand (the disk throttles the three 0.327-mMag jump/boost ticks, which the game cannot throttle; the 0.026/tick air correction capacity is fully consumed by the saturated intended inputs) and sticks at 2.6e-2..5.3e-2 on j003 (176 interior ticks). An 8-round SLP from the tracked anchor stalls: the linearized model itself reports the best local point still ~9e-3 infeasible, because chatter is a nonlocal alternation outside any small trust region. Naive full-modulus decode of the disk point is equally dead (thousand 1.0-block viol, j716 5.5e-2).
2. **What works: make the SOLVE full-modulus, then decode directly (no realization gap exists at all).** Two implementations both measured landing: (a) **greedy chord-cut arc narrowing** on the disk SOCP: for each throttled tick add `cos(mu)ux + sin(mu)uz >= mMag cos(delta)` centered on the current direction, re-solve, re-center, shrink delta 0.7x, until slack < 1e-4 mMag; this is DiskSocpKernel plus one linear row per tick, iterated, i.e. pure Java; (b) the exact **sphere QCQP** (COPT research oracle only; j003 solves OPTIMAL gap 0.0 in 0.33 s). M1e reframes from "chatter rounding DP" to "arc narrowing to full modulus + the polish ladder". Architectural bonus: the chord cut is the same device the M2a B&B branches on, so FAST = greedy narrowing (no backtracking) and CERTIFIED = branching the same cuts; one mechanism family, two search disciplines.

### The polish ladder that closes e-3 -> 0 (each rung measured necessary)

- **Anchor margins alone oscillate at e-4 and never land** (thousand rounds 1-11: maxViol bounced 6e-5..3.3e-4 across re-anchors), confirming the H7/j154 verdict at per-tick scale.
- The ladder that lands: **lexicographic SLP** (maximize min slack capped at 1e-4, then maximize objective; continuous per-tick dyaw in a trust region, shrink 0.4x on replay regression) -> **free-start translation window** (rigid FreeP0 shift is byte-exact to ~1e-12; per-axis interval intersection of measured violations) -> **gate-banded integer bucket walk** (steps of 0.0054931640625 deg, W=2, move budget 6 halved on regression; gate-band rows keep every carry velocity on its measured side of the inertia threshold via friction couplings with pattern cuts) -> **objective walk** (same MIP, maximize objective subject to min slack >= 2e-6, budget doubled while replay gain matches prediction within 30%).
- **Gate-pattern fold: 1 round to the fixed point on all four instances** (patterns are tiny: 2-13 zero events), extracted from the driver's own replays (`zeroX[t] = |velX[t]| < thr`, combined-norm form for modern). The fold is what dropped thousand from 0.42 viol to 8.7e-5 in one round.

### Traps measured this session (build notes)

- Bucket steps applied to continuous yaws can miss sine-table boundaries entirely: j003 walk rounds replayed literally unchanged maxViol while the LP predicted progress. The leaf must operate on bucket indices (snap to centers first), which confirms M1d as specified (window scan, never nearest-snap, bucket-indexed).
- The gate-band trust region is what makes the walk safe: without it the walk flips gate events and replays 100x off prediction (thousand: predicted min slack 8.6e-5, replayed 3.6e-2).
- The modern combined gate was approximated per-axis (3e-3 box) in the band rows; harmless here (j003 has 2 gate events) but gate-dense modern captures need the exact combined form.
- j1150-hpk solves 3.3e-3 above the recorded human against the in-repo hpk spec: those walls are looser than the PRECISE inputs_gone spec. Fixed-schedule expects should compile the PRECISE specs, as the regression section already says.
- Objective walk terminates at a bucket-lattice local optimum ("no move proposed"): the 2.2e-6 gap to the continuous bound is not certified. Certification stays M2a's job.

Artifacts: driver `research/copt/inner_fixed.py`; runs `data/m0t6-*` (thousand), `data/m0j716a-*`, `data/m0j1150-*` (knife edges), `data/m0j003s-*` / `m0j003o-*` (sphere path), `m0j003c2-*` (chord path); warm checks `m0-thousand-warm-*`, `m0j716-warmcheck-*`, `m0j1150wc-warmcheck-*`. Wall clock per loop is tens of seconds, dominated by JVM startup per replay (in-engine these replays are in-process).

Next: the step-1 component inventory (stage 1), posted as the following comment.
